key_insight: ETCH-X combines a composable-dataset training strategy with a modular fitting architecture (coarse global fit + local expressive refiners) to simultaneously achieve robust alignment to clothed, noisy, or partial scans and preserve fine details (hands, face).
problem_solved: Brings together local expressiveness and global robustness for fitting parametric body models (e.g., SMPL-X) to real-world 3D scans of clothed humans, handling clothing, pose variation, occlusion, and sensor noise without needing one monolithic dataset.
method: Composable datasets: merge heterogeneous data sources (scans, mocap, partial depth, 2D annotations, synthetic clothed examples) via lightweight domain adapters and targeted augmentation so training covers diverse clothing, poses, and noise.

Modular fitting pipeline: a coarse global estimator fits the parametric body (SMPL-X backbone) and then specialized local refinement modules recover high-frequency details for hands, face, and fine shape using attention/residual fields.

Hybrid supervision & losses: multi-task training with geometric (point-to-surface, silhouette), semantic (keypoints/landmarks), and robustness losses plus differentiable registration to tolerate partial/noisy inputs.
impact: Enables practitioners to produce reliable, expressive body fits from real-world clothed scans without collecting a single massive curated dataset—improving downstream animation, virtual try-on, and AR/VR pipelines while reducing data engineering effort.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: composable-dataset inputs → domain adapters → coarse global fit → local detail refiners → final SMPL‑X-aligned mesh

paper_title: ETCH-X: Robustify Expressive Body Fitting to Clothed Humans with Composable Datasets
paper_authors: Xiaoben Li, Jingyi Wu, Zeyu Cai, Yu Siyuan, Boqian Li
